info.name: Applicant Service
info.description:
Applicant Service — Team 16, "Student ID, please" (FAF.PAD21.1).

The service owns the identity of the people trying to get into the university Discord server. Every applicant exists twice: the profile they claim, which this API serves, and the profile that is true, which never leaves the service except inside the applicant.initialized event.

Lab 4: in the running system every request reaches the service through the Message Broker, on its queue requests.applicant, and the events travel through the broker too. The broker speaks gRPC, which this collection cannot, so the folders below call the REST port directly - the same router the broker's requests are dispatched to - and "Through the Gateway" shows the one player route that stays.

Run the requests top to bottom: "Next applicant" stores the new applicant_id in a collection variable, and the requests after it reuse it.

Set `base_url` to where the service is listening (http://localhost:8081 by default).

request.description: Answers 200 whenever the process is serving. It deliberately does not check Postgres: a liveness probe that fails on a dependency restarts a healthy container because somebody else is having a bad day.

Reports whether the service can do useful work. The database is the only hard dependency. `components.event_relay` says whether applicant.initialized can be pushed at all, and `consumers.<name>` how many deliveries still wait for each consumer (`pending`) or were refused with 422 (`parked`).

item.name: Through the Gateway
item.description: Lab 4: the Gateway forwards only the routes a player uses (CPR README "Gateway"); every other route of this service answers 404 there, and the services reach it through the Message Broker instead. For this service one route stays: GET /api/v1/applicant/applicants/{id}, with a player's `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`, which this folder's pre-request script mints for `player_id` with `jwt_secret`. The Gateway hands it to the broker, which delivers it to the least loaded instance; the service sees `X-Player-Id` and no credential. `GET /api/v1/applicant/health` stays public.

exec: // Player tokens, signed the way Player Service signs them: HS256 with JWT_SECRET, `sub` = the
// player's id, `iat` and `exp`. The Gateway verifies the signature, so `jwt_secret` must be the
// JWT_SECRET of the Gateway being called (gateway-service/.env).
return header + '.' + payload + '.' + b64url(CryptoJS.HmacSHA256(header + '.' + payload, secret));
pm.collectionVariables.set('player_token', mint({ sub: sub, iat: now, exp: now + 3600 }, secret));

item.name: Lab 3: status and Service Discovery
item.description: Lab 3: several copies of the service share one database, register themselves with Service Discovery and report their load on GET /status. Logs are JSON lines carrying `instance_id` and `request_id`, so `docker compose logs applicant-service` shows which copy answered each request.

request.description: GET /status at the root, next to /health: this instance's health and load, in the shape every Lab 3 component shares. Service Discovery calls it directly, not through the Gateway, every 10 s with a 2 s timeout. No credential, and it is outside the concurrent task limit, so a saturated instance answers it (busy) instead of refusing it with a 429 (broken). 200 `up`, or 503 `degraded` with the same body when the database does not answer. `in_flight` / `max_concurrent_tasks` is the load; Service Discovery alerts at 80 %. This request calls this instance directly.

exec: pm.test('200 OK, or 503 when the database is down', () => pm.expect([200, 503]).to.include(pm.response.code));

item.name: Status is not routed through the Gateway

request.description: Lab 4: the Gateway forwards only player routes, so /status - for Service Discovery inside the network - answers 404 there.

Every copy of the service registers itself with Service Discovery (PUT /api/v1/instances/{instance_id}) right after its listener is up and repeats it every 5 s; a copy that stops deregisters (DELETE). This is the list the Gateway reads every 5 s to share requests round-robin: `up` instances only. Needs Service Discovery (published on 8090 in the team stack). With `docker compose up -d --scale applicant-service=3` it lists three.
